dedupe_keys.name: ifpri integrated cadre harmonise household food security and coping datasets for niger chad mali and burkina faso 2018 to 2023

description: These datasets integrate and standardise the household food security surveys run twice a year for the Cadre Harmonisé, the food insecurity classification used in West Africa and the Sahel. They were published by the International Food Policy Research Institute on Harvard Dataverse in 2025, one dataset per country; this record covers Niger, with sister datasets for Chad, Mali and Burkina Faso. Surveys are held before the lean season, around February and March, and at its end or the start of harvest, around September and October, and are generally representative at the second administrative level. Indicators include the Food Consumption Score, the Household Dietary Diversity Score and coping behaviours. IFPRI adds covariate shocks in each area between rounds in five domains: conflict and political violence, food price anomalies, long-term climate hazards, rainy season performance and extreme weather events. The Niger files are tab-separated tables of about 120 MB, free to download under custom Dataverse terms. Caveats: survey designs vary by round and country, and shock variables are derived from external sources. Simulation uses: household food security responses to shocks for food supply and humanitarian response models. Related records: the Cadre Harmonisé and IPC country data (data-cadre-harmonise-west-central-africa) give the area classifications, and WFP Food Consumption Score data (data-wfp-food-consumption-score-38-countries) are a related series.
